activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The matrix $T$ is given below. Let ${t}_{1}$, ${t}_{2}$, and ${t}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $T.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${t}_{3}={x}_{1}{t}_{1}+{x}_{2}{t}_{2}.$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $T$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -4 \\ 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{12}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(T)$ is ${{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}.$

Therefore, we conclude that $\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\text{}}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$
